entities.name: Biglycan core protein
observations: Recombinant human biglycan core protein protected primary neonatal rat cardiomyocytes from simulated ischemia/reperfusion injury.

The protein core was protective, whereas dermatan sulfate was not significantly protective and chondroitin sulfate worsened injury; this supports the core as the active component rather than glycosaminoglycan chains.

entities.name: TLR4
observations: Pharmacologic TLR4 blockade abolished recombinant biglycan core protein-mediated cardioprotection in the neonatal cardiomyocyte simulated ischemia/reperfusion model.
The study supports functional TLR4 dependence but did not provide genetic TLR4 knockout validation.

entities.name: Cardiomyocytes
observations: Primary neonatal rat cardiomyocytes exposed to simulated ischemia/reperfusion were the directly tested cardiac model.
The retrieved evidence did not establish efficacy in an in-vivo infarct model or whole-heart TLR4 knockout.

entities.name: PMID:27515282
observations: In primary neonatal rat cardiomyocytes subjected to simulated ischemia/reperfusion, recombinant human biglycan core protein reduced cell death and injury-associated necrosis, apoptosis, mitochondrial membrane-potential loss, and autophagy changes.
TLR4, IRAK1/4, ERK, JNK, or p38 inhibition abolished protection; biglycan core protein also induced early ERK1 phosphorylation and increased Akt phosphorylation and nitric-oxide production.
The study did not report TLR4 knockout or a direct NF-kB requirement test.

entities.name: Biglycan TLR4 cardioprotection
observations: In vitro pharmacologic evidence indicates that TLR4 signaling is functionally required for biglycan core protein cytoprotection in cardiomyocytes, with downstream IRAK/MAPK and Akt/NO signaling.
